reviewer: Kimi independent actual visual comparison of the exact 65x67 source PNG, enlarged existing source-page 15 and targeted source-note crop, complete unchanged 2048x2048 raw RGBA and native note/right-edge crop, full white/cyan/alpha sheet and evidence, and unchanged naiwa.png; checked two silver cap elements, covered hair, brows, clean-shaven face, one mouth, three-quarter presentation, two pale collar tabs without tie, collar fit, backplate, note rows and right-edge tab.

remaining_reasons: The returned native note has THREE distinct upper gray-mark rows, while the enlarged original has only its existing TWO compact upper rows. Remove the invented third row and restore only the source-scale two-row upper footprint and original blank areas.

The original small dark right-edge note tab is replaced by a triangular paper fold/notch in the native return. Restore the source's compact dark tab in its original position and form rather than substituting a crease or torn notch.
entries.positive_observation: The dark gray-green peaked cap retains two silver-toned front insignia elements, silver braid and a glossy black visor. Hairline and most sideburns remain covered, with dark brows, no glasses, no moustache or beard and one stern closed mouth. The three-quarter bust presentation, tight crop and strong detail-preserving visor shadow remain. The dark field-gray high-collared tunic keeps two pale-gray rectangular collar tabs and a dark central collar opening without a tie. The rounded chin meets a short broad fitted collar without a stalk or pinching. The dark neutral gray-olive photographic backplate and thin dark frame remain opaque. Full white/cyan comparisons show no visible interior holes, lost backing or working-matte ring; the third note row and right-edge tab substitution remain separate visible rejection reasons.
entries.visible_limitations: Exact tiny cap/collar insignia motifs and note glyphs are unreadable at 65x67 and are not rejection grounds. The rejection relies on clearly resolved three-versus-two note rows and the changed native right-edge structure, not on interpreting small writing, head-direction guessing or alpha numbers.
